title: Nvidia Resists Huang Comeback Despite Trump’s Support
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to Reuters, despite a growing campaign backed by prominent technology executives and supportive comments from US President Donald Trump.

The campaign has intensified a leadership crisis at the AI chipmaker, putting pressure on directors as they oversee investigations and search for a permanent successor.

Trump said on November 16 that he “would certainly not mind” seeing Huang return. His remarks added political weight to an effort whose listed supporters include Elon Musk, Replit chief executive Amjad Masad and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney.

Reuters reported that more than 180,200 people had signed a petition seeking Huang’s reinstatement. Thousands identified themselves as Nvidia employees, although the campaign cautioned that professional affiliations were self-reported and had not been independently verified.

Supporters want Huang restored while an independent investigation establishes the facts. However, three people told Reuters that the board was not weighing his return.

Nvidia’s regulatory filing states that directors accepted Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and board member on November 11, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim chief executive.

His departure followed revelations about personal relationships, including one with a Chinese businesswoman whose alleged intelligence connections remain under scrutiny. Allegations about those connections should not be treated as established findings.

The dispute matters because it tests how Nvidia balances the influence of its co-founder against board oversight and continuity. Huang’s relationships span employees, customers, suppliers and government.

For directors, public support does not resolve the questions under investigation. Their immediate challenge is maintaining confidence in Nvidia’s operations while ensuring leadership decisions follow a credible process. The campaign demonstrates Huang’s enduring influence, but the board’s reported position indicates that popularity alone will not determine whether he returns to lead the company through its next phase.
